reviews.one_line_contribution: A same-backbone, same-pool measurement showing that retrieved agent experience removes more total episode tokens (by converting 30-step timeouts into ~12-step successes) than the ~430 tokens it injects, so the weights-versus-context break-even horizon N* changes by >2x depending only on whether cost is counted as injected tokens, total episode tokens, or measured GPU-seconds.
reviews.closest_prior_work: 2512.02543 (VERIFIED via the literature command; S2 title 'Inference-Time Distillation: Cost-Efficient Agents Without Fine-Tuning or Manual Prompt Engineering', 2025-12-02) is the nearest: it already shifts a cost-accuracy Pareto frontier on ALFWorld with dynamic in-context demonstrations at 2.5x lower cost and computes a teacher-vs-student break-even, so 'demonstrations can lower total agent cost' is not itself new; it does not, however, run a parametric arm or attribute the saving to episode shortening, which is the proposal's actual wedge. Second threat, found by my search and VERIFIED: PANDO 2605.24785 (2026-05-24), an online skill-distillation agent that introduces 'three trajectory-level efficiency metrics to make efficiency visible beyond terminal success' plus cache-aware prompting — this directly undercuts the proposal's framing premise that the literature counts injected tokens 'and stops there'. MemCon 2607.13591 (VERIFIED, 2026-07-15) likewise reports improved success *while reducing token use* from adaptive retrieval. None of these builds the weights route from the same pool or reports a break-even with a CI, so novelty survives, but it is narrower than the abstract claims: the new thing is the same-backbone break-even and the convention-sensitivity number, not the observation that memory can be token-positive.
reviews.strongest_objection: The headline result is close to arithmetic on data the program already has, and the two flagship predictions are mutually corrosive. (a) P1: in ReAct the prompt is the growing history, so per-episode prompt tokens scale roughly quadratically in steps; the brief's own Measurement A has k=0 failing ~46% of episodes by exhausting the 30-step cap while k=3 finishes in ~12. A 30-step vs 12-step episode differs by several-fold in total tokens, against 430 injected. P1 cannot plausibly fail, and its stated falsifier (pooled paired difference > 0) is unreachable; the pre-registered '>=25% fall on multi-step types' is a threshold the setup will clear by a wide margin. The brief's own rule against predictions entailed by the setup bites here. (b) Worse, if P1 holds then c_context < c_student under exactly the accounting convention the paper advocates, so the denominator (c_context - c_student) of N* is negative and the headline estimand is undefined or negative rather than '2x different'. The proposal only handles the undefined case where the student cannot reach accuracy A; it never says what N* means when context is both more accurate and cheaper. So either memory dominates outright and there is no break-even horizon to report under the total-token convention (the interesting half of P3 evaporates into 'N* = infinity'), or P1 is weaker than claimed. A skeptical AC reads this as a well-instrumented logging exercise whose conclusion is fixed before the run, with the residual contribution being a Pareto plot for one environment whose 30-step cap is an arbitrary harness parameter — as the proposal's own Risk Factor (1) and (3) concede.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: 1) Fix the estimand: replace 'N* moves by >2x' with a signed per-episode cost difference at iso-accuracy (with CI) plus an explicit 'context dominates, no finite break-even' region, and pre-register how the convention comparison is reported when a denominator is negative — the convention-sensitivity claim should be about the *ordering and sign* of the substrate comparison, not a ratio of horizons that may not exist. 2) Demote P1 to a calibration measurement (it is near-certain) and make the confirmatory claim the one that is genuinely open: whether the memory-free student inherits the shortening (P2) and whether the substrate ordering survives prefix caching and batching (the GPU-second convention), which is the only convention where the answer is not predictable from step counts. 3) Add a non-retrieval procedure control (below). 4) Report total prompt-token growth per step so the quadratic-history mechanism is separated from the step-count mechanism; otherwise 'memory pays for its own tokens' is a statement about ReAct history growth, not about memory. 5) Cut the evaluation to fit the budget (see feasibility) or extend the stated schedule.
reviews.missing_baseline: A static procedural-instruction arm: a hand-written or once-compiled per-task-type procedure (clean/heat/cool-then-place) inserted in the system prompt, token-matched to k=3 and fully prefix-cached, with no retrieval. The decoy arms control for length and relevance but not for the possibility that *any* correct procedure text converts the timeouts — which would make the result about procedure knowledge, not about retrieved experience, and would give a context route whose marginal token cost is ~0 under prefix caching, dominating both the k=3 arm and every student on the Pareto plot (the program's own round-1 idea 'memory_or_instruction' is exactly this contrast). Secondary omission on the weights side: an efficiency-trained baseline that directly optimizes what the paper measures, e.g. DEPO 2511.15392 (dual-efficiency preference optimization minimizing step count and tokens); it is the natural competitor for 'make the memory-free student's episodes shorter' and its absence makes P2 a comparison against an unoptimized student only.
reviews.preprint_collision: No verified collision. The proposal's own check is above average for this round — four queries reported with IDs, correct channel disclosure, and it verified 2512.02543, whose S2 title I confirmed exactly as quoted. My own searches (all channel (a), the s2cli literature command; WebSearch unavailable this session, WebFetch never used): (1) 'retrieved experience memory reduces episode length total token cost agent' --recent -> 2607.10608, 2608.00017, 2605.11212, 2606.05684, 2606.05646, 2606.04536, 2605.12978, 2605.12493 — none measures net episode-token savings from retrieved experience; (2) 'break-even amortization fine-tuning versus in-context learning inference cost crossover' -> 2512.02543, 2608.08744, 2601.03822, 2305.16938 — closest remains 2512.02543, no weights arm; (3) 'few-shot demonstrations shorten agent trajectories fewer steps token savings efficiency' --recent -> 2605.24785 PANDO, 2509.23586 AgentDiet, 2511.15392 DEPO, 2604.00824; (4) 'memory retrieval pays for itself net token savings agent inference cost accounting' --recent -> 2607.13591 MemCon, 2601.02553 SimpleMem, 2605.30690 ElasticMem, 2606.06036 MRAgent — several report memory systems that cut token cost, none as a substrate cost comparison; (5) 'parametric memory versus in-context memory same backbone cost matched comparison ALFWorld' --recent -> 2607.27919, 2605.30260, 2602.19320, 2608.17050 — nothing cost-matched; (6) 'RAG versus fine-tuning cost tradeoff total cost of ownership inference tokens training compute' -> 2401.08406, 2507.07634, 2505.20266 — the classic RAG-vs-finetune cost framing the proposal never cites, none on agent episodes; (7) 'timeout failures step budget exhaustion agent success shorter trajectories with retrieved demonstrations ALFWorld' --recent -> nothing on point. IDs I verified with `paper`: 2512.02543 (title as quoted), 2607.21051 (S2 title 'Sample-Efficient Learning from Agent Experience', abstract does name Experience Distillation, so the citation is real though the proposal cites it under the method name rather than the paper title), 2605.24785, 2607.13591. 2607.21503 is corroborated by the novelty card (same title and date). IDs the proposal leans on that I did NOT verify: 2512.10696 (ReMe), 2607.28272 (MemHarness), 2605.01214, 2607.01480, 2604.02268, 2602.04942, 2607.29468, 2606.29502 — the argument does not hinge on any single one, but the claim '2512.02543 is the only amortization analysis' rests partly on unverified negatives. Weakness in the check: it searched only for its own positive claim and missed the two papers that most weaken its framing premise (2605.24785, 2607.13591) and the RAG-vs-fine-tuning cost literature entirely.
